title: When words run out
job: Paraphrase, ask what something means, repair a misunderstanding
verifiedBy: Claude Opus 5 — LLM review, authorised by repo owner

allowedTenses: presente, L1-M6's - every finite verb of the ten except two
tu imperative, L4-M1's, now carrying attached pronouns: dimmi, ripetimelo, spiegami
passato prossimo on an owned participle: non ho capito, hai detto

rules.text: THE PRONOUN'S POSITION IS DECIDED BY THE VERB FORM AND BY NOTHING ELSE. It ATTACHES, welded on the end, to an infinitive, to a tu imperative and to a gerund: dimmi, ripetimelo, spiegami. It stands BEFORE a finite verb: me lo dici, me lo ripeti. dimmi and me lo dici are the same words in the same relation, and only the shape of the verb moves the pronoun. Not politeness, not emphasis, not meaning.

WHEN TWO PRONOUNS MEET, THE INDIRECT ONE COMES FIRST AND ITS VOWEL CHANGES TO E. mi lo is not a form; me lo is. Same for te lo and ce lo. And gli plus lo does not sit side by side at all - it fuses into one written word, glielo, which is why it looks like a word rather than a pair.

NE IS THE PRONOUN FOR OF IT AND OF THEM, AND IT JOINS THE SAME SYSTEM. Non ne parlo mai, I never talk about it. It attaches to the same three verb forms the others attach to, and it survives frozen in che ne so - literally what do I know of it, and in practice a shrug.

THE PARAPHRASE KIT IS FOUR PHRASES AND ONE JOKER, AND NOTHING IN IT IS NEW COMMUNICATIVELY. una specie di - a sort of. quella cosa che - that thing that. come si dice - how do you say. che vuol dire - what does it mean. The joker is coso, the word for a thing whose word you have lost; it is informal and it is exactly English thingy.

THE TWO THINGS ENGLISH GIVES YOU NO HELP WITH. The vowel change has no logic to offer and no analogue: me lo is simply the form and mi lo is not Italian. And glielo is ONE word for to him, to her AND to them, so three English pronouns collapse into one - there is no feminine version to hunt for, and hunting for it is the commonest wasted hour at this level.

WHAT THIS MODULE NAMES AND DOES NOT TEACH. Attachment to the Lei imperative - me lo dica - is a fourth position, and every polite repair here stays on the finite frame instead: me lo può ripetere. The ci of place with attachment - andarci, restarci - is named here and left; the course closes at this level and a named absence is better than half a system. L5-M1's farcela and cavarsela are this machine already welded shut, and they are not bought a second time.

sentences.display: Come si dice questo in italiano?
sentences.cue: How do you say this in Italian?
sentences.literal: How one says this in Italian?

words.note: Three tokens, one key, sitting on L5-M3's si dice. It is the single most useful sentence opener a learner owns, because it asks for the word without needing it.

sentences.trap: si dice is impersonal - one says. Turning it into come dici tu asks how YOU personally say it, which is a different and much stranger question.
sentences.sound: CO-me si DI-ce, four light syllables, nothing stressed hard.

variations.cue: How do you say it in Italian?
variations.changed: the thing left unnamed, pointed at instead
the language left out, when it is obvious

mistake.why: come dici is how do YOU say it, and it sounds like a challenge. The impersonal si is what makes the question about the language rather than about the person.

sentences.usage: Mid-conversation, when the word you need has not arrived.
sentences.mnemonic: si dice: one says, so nobody has to.

words.note: Literally what does it want to say, which is how Italian says mean. Learned whole: vuol here is not a shortened voglio and does not conjugate with you.
The word for a word. It is what you point at when you cannot repeat it, and it turns a blank stare into a question somebody can answer.

sentences.trap: vuol dire is about the word, not the speaker. Che vuoi dire? asks what YOU mean by that, which is a challenge; che vuol dire asks what the word means.
sentences.sound: ke vwol DI-re. pa-RO-la, stress on RO.

variations.changed: the bare question, pointing at what was just said

variations.cue: I did not understand this word
variations.changed: the same problem stated instead of asked

mistake.why: Not wrong, but nobody says it. The frozen shape is vuol dire, with the e gone, and that is the form to learn.

sentences.usage: Stopping somebody on one word rather than on the whole sentence.
sentences.mnemonic: the word WANTS to say something.

sentences.display: Non ho capito: me lo puoi ripetere più piano?
sentences.cue: I did not understand: can you say it again more slowly?
sentences.literal: Not I have understood: to-me it you can to repeat more slowly?

words.note: The standard repair, in the passato prossimo rather than the present: Italian reports the failure as a completed event. ho capito on its own is got it.
Two pronouns in the order Italian keeps: indirect first, and mi becomes me in front of lo. Before a finite verb they stand apart from it, as here.
piano is both slowly and softly, and the request is heard as either. It is what you add when the words were fine and the speed was not.

sentences.trap: Non capisco says I do not understand in general; non ho capito says I missed that one. The repair Italians use is the past one.
sentences.sound: non o ca-PI-to. me lo PWOI ri-PE-te-re. pyu PIA-no.

variations.changed: the request without the reason

variations.display: Me lo puoi ripetere più piano?
variations.cue: Can you say it again more slowly?
variations.changed: the whole repair in one question
the admission alone, which is often enough

mistake.display: Non ho capito: mi lo puoi ripetere più piano?
mistake.why: mi lo is not a form. In front of lo the pronoun mi becomes me, with no reason available and no exception.

sentences.usage: The first thing to say when a sentence went past too fast.
sentences.mnemonic: mi + lo = me lo. The vowel bends, the order does not.

sentences.display: Dimmi tutto, e poi dimmelo ancora
sentences.cue: Tell me everything, and then tell it to me again
sentences.literal: Tell-me all, and then tell-it-to-me again

words.note: The tu imperative of dire with the pronoun welded on. The doubled m is the weld: di plus mi, written as one word, and this is the shape English tell me already has.
Both pronouns attached, in the order rule 1 gives: me before lo, all of it on the end of the verb. One word, three pieces.

sentences.trap: dimmi is an imperative and me lo dici is a statement, but the words are identical - only the verb form moved the pronouns. That is the whole system in one pair.
sentences.sound: DIM-mi, double m held. DIM-me-lo, stress stays on the first syllable.

variations.changed: one pronoun instead of two
the doubled form alone

mistake.why: Attachment is not optional on a tu imperative. The three pieces are written as one word, dimmelo, and split apart they read as nothing at all.

sentences.usage: Asking a friend to go over something once more.

sentences.display: Ripetimi il numero. Ripetimelo, per favore
sentences.cue: Say the number to me again. Say it to me again, please

words.note: L2-M1's ripetere as a tu imperative with mi welded on. The stress does not move to the pronoun: it stays where the verb had it.
Five syllables and one word. The two pronouns follow rule 1's order even after they attach, so me comes before lo here exactly as it does before a finite verb.

sentences.trap: Both forms are tu. To somebody you call Lei the repair goes on a finite verb instead - me lo può ripetere - because attaching to the polite imperative is a position this course does not teach.
sentences.sound: ri-PE-ti-mi. ri-PE-ti-me-lo - five syllables, and the stress is still on PE.

variations.cue: Say the number to me again
variations.changed: the thing named rather than pronounced

variations.cue: Say it to me again, please
variations.changed: both pronouns, with the thing left understood

mistake.why: Two errors from one cause: the pronouns must attach to a tu imperative, and once lo is there the number cannot be named again.

sentences.usage: On the phone, when a number went by too fast.
sentences.mnemonic: ripeti + me + lo, in that order, welded.

sentences.display: Spiegami quella cosa che hai detto: voglio capire
sentences.cue: Explain that thing you said to me: I want to understand
sentences.literal: Explain-to-me that thing that you have said: I want to understand

words.note: L4-M2's spiegare as a tu imperative with mi attached. No doubling here - the m of mi is the only one, because spiega already ends in a vowel.

words.cue: that thing that, you know the one
words.note: The paraphraser's frame: it points at something whose name you do not have and hands the naming back to the other person.
The infinitive behind L4-M5's capisco and L3-M10's capito. After voglio, dopo and per it is this form the sentence needs.

sentences.trap: dimmi doubles its m and spiegami does not. The doubling belongs to the four short imperatives - di', da', fa', sta', va' - and not to the rule.
sentences.sound: SPIE-ga-mi, stress stays on SPIE. ca-PI-re.

variations.display: Spiegami quella cosa che hai detto
variations.cue: Explain that thing you said to me
variations.changed: the request without the reason
the reason on its own

mistake.display: Spiegammi quella cosa che hai detto
mistake.why: No double m on this one. spiega ends in a vowel already, so the pronoun simply joins it: spiegami.

sentences.usage: Asking somebody to unpack something they said, without admitting which part was lost.
sentences.mnemonic: that THING that - and let them supply the word.

sentences.display: Come si chiama quel coso? È una specie di pane
sentences.cue: What is that thingy called? It is a sort of bread
sentences.literal: How itself calls that thing? It is a species of bread

words.note: Three tokens over L1-M1's si chiama, which introduced people. The same words ask the name of an object, and this is the question that unblocks a paraphrase.
The word for a thing whose word has gone. Masculine for an object, informal, and never written in anything formal - but heard constantly.

words.cue: a sort of, a kind of
words.note: The paraphrase frame itself: name the nearest category you DO know and let the hearer close the gap. It is what keeps a conversation moving.

sentences.trap: coso is not cosa in the masculine. cosa is the ordinary word for thing; coso is the one you reach for when the name has gone, and it is informal.
sentences.sound: CO-me si CHIA-ma. CO-so. U-na SPE-cie di.

variations.changed: the question alone

variations.cue: It is a sort of bread
variations.changed: the paraphrase alone, offered rather than asked

mistake.why: coso is masculine whatever it stands for. The feminine would be cosa, which is the ordinary noun and not this word at all.

sentences.usage: In a shop or a kitchen, pointing at something whose name you never learned.
sentences.mnemonic: a sort of X beats no X at all.

sentences.display: Te lo dico io: glielo spiego domani
sentences.cue: I am telling you: I will explain it to him tomorrow
sentences.literal: To-you it I say I: to-him-it I explain tomorrow

words.note: ti becomes te in front of lo, exactly as mi becomes me. Te lo dico io, with the io added at the end, is how Italian says take it from me.

words.cue: it to him, it to her, it to them
words.note: One written word for three English pronouns. gli plus lo fused, and there is no feminine version - glielo covers her too.

sentences.trap: glielo is not gli lo and it is not a le form. Whether the person is a man, a woman or several people, the word is the same one.
sentences.sound: te lo DI-co I-o. GLIE-lo - the gli as in figlio, then a plain lo.

variations.changed: the first half, which stands alone as a phrase

variations.cue: I will explain it to him tomorrow
variations.changed: the second half alone

mistake.why: le plus lo never stand apart. The pair has exactly one written form, glielo, and it is used for her as much as for him.

sentences.usage: Promising to pass something on, or vouching for something yourself.
sentences.mnemonic: gli + lo fuse; nothing else about them changes.

sentences.display: Che ne so? Non ne parlo mai
sentences.cue: How would I know? I never talk about it
sentences.literal: What of-it I know? Not of-it I talk never

words.cue: how should I know, search me
words.note: A frozen shrug that happens to contain the pronoun this sentence teaches. Learned whole; it is not a real question and expects no answer.

words.cue: of it, of them, about it
words.note: The pronoun for the of-phrase. Non ne parlo is I do not talk about it, and the thing itself is never named again once ne has stood in for it.

sentences.trap: ne is not the English none and not a negative. It replaces di plus a thing, and the negation in this sentence comes from non, as always.
sentences.sound: ke ne SO, three syllables and the weight at the end. non ne PAR-lo MAI.

variations.changed: the shrug alone
the pronoun doing ordinary work

mistake.why: ne IS the di phrase, so it cannot follow di. It goes in front of the finite verb, like the other pronouns of this module.

sentences.usage: Refusing a question you genuinely cannot answer, without sounding sharp.

sentences.display: Nel senso che intendevo un'altra cosa
sentences.cue: Meaning that I meant something else
sentences.literal: In the sense that I intended an other thing

words.cue: meaning that, in the sense that
words.note: The repair frame: it reopens what you just said so you can restate it. Italians use it constantly, and it buys a whole second try at a sentence.
The imperfetto, because what you meant was true all along rather than done at a moment. It is the verb for undoing a misunderstanding you caused.

sentences.trap: intendevo is what you MEANT; ho detto is what you said. Repairing with ho detto argues about the words, which is the fight this phrase exists to avoid.
sentences.sound: nel SEN-so ke. in-ten-DE-vo, stress on DE.

variations.changed: the repair without the frame

variations.display: Nel senso che non ho capito
variations.cue: Meaning that I did not understand
variations.changed: the frame carrying an admission instead

mistake.display: Nel senso che ho inteso un'altra cosa
mistake.why: The passato prossimo makes it a completed act of understanding, which is a claim about the other person's sentence. The imperfetto keeps it about your own intention.

sentences.usage: Taking back a sentence that landed wrong, before it turns into an argument.
sentences.mnemonic: nel senso che opens the door back in.
